lessons.title: Devoir + infinitive
lessons.objective: Devoir + infinitive: Conjugate devoir for the person and keep the second verb in the infinitive.
lessons.explanation:
Conjugate devoir for the person and keep the second verb in the infinitive. It expresses a personal obligation. To say you do not have to, use je n'ai pas besoin de: je ne dois pas means I must not.
Je dois ouvrir le café à sept heures. — I have to open the café at seven.
Ma collègue doit apporter le pain. — My coworker has to bring the bread.
lessons.speakingPrompt: You and a French-speaking classmate are discussing opening a small café. Conjugate devoir for the person and keep the second verb in the infinitive. It expresses a personal obligation. To say you do not have to, use je n'ai pas besoin de: je ne dois pas means I must not. Ask for the missing detail, respond to the partner, clarify one misunderstanding, and agree on the next step. Use examples from the reading and your own details. Explain the grammar in English if asked.

items.note: Only the s of dois is silent: it sounds like dwa. Je ne dois pas means I must not.
On its own, dix is pronounced dees. Before a vowel or silent h the x links as a z: dix heures sounds like dee-zeur.

lessons.objective: Être sur le point de + infinitive: Use être sur le point de + infinitive to describe an action on the verge of happening.

lessons.title: Si + present: open conditions
lessons.objective: Si + present: open conditions: For an open future condition, French uses si + present, and the result can be in the future, the present or an imperative.
lessons.explanation:

lessons.title: C'est pour ça que / C'est pourquoi vs parce que
lessons.objective: C'est pour ça que / C'est pourquoi vs parce que: C'est pour ça que (spoken) and c'est pourquoi (written) introduce the consequence of something already stated; donc works too.
lessons.explanation:

lessons.objective: En + present participle (gérondif): on / while doing: En + present participle (gérondif) expresses an action that happens at the same time as, or just before, the main action: en arrivant, en le lisant.

En arrivant au bureau, j'ai vu un mot sur la porte. — On arriving at the office, I saw a note on the door.

lessons.title: Aussi … que / autant (de) … que: equality
lessons.objective: Aussi … que / autant (de) … que: equality: Use aussi + adjective or adverb + que to say two things are equal: aussi calme que, aussi bien que.
lessons.explanation:
Use aussi + adjective or adverb + que to say two things are equal: aussi calme que, aussi bien que. Use autant de + noun + que for quantity (autant de chaises que) and autant que after a verb (étudier autant que).

grammarChecks.explanation: The passé composé is formed with the present of avoir or être plus the past participle: nous avons préparé, il est arrivé. Most verbs take avoir; verbs of movement or change and pronominal verbs take être, and the participle agrees with the subject. The plus-que-parfait (nous avions mis) places an action before another past point.
